maps.name: Blackwell Fields
maps.layout: Rural Southern California badlands at sunset (Kern County). Large, open map with minimal buildings outside objective areas; a garage, military depot, hangars, small outposts, active oil pumpjacks, many hills and trenches, a map-bisecting east-west road, and an active wildfire that damages players. Six Conquest flags: Salvage Lot, Homestead, Site Office, Relay Station, Oil Fields, Military Base. Small modes use two 'Misfire' variants (east hangars / west garage).
maps.notes: Documented 'long, open sightlines broken up only by hills', 'cover is minimal so expect to be shot from almost anywhere', snipers and tanks dominate; spawn-to-spawn sightlines. CQB confined to depot/scrapyard/hangar objectives. Vehicles: all types including jets. Not in Escalation rotation; EA-confirmed rework planned for Season 5 with New Sobek City. inferred: weights reflect open dominant with LONG bias.

maps.name: Cairo Bazaar
maps.layout: Reimagined Grand Bazaar (BF3) in central Cairo; urban marketplace of alleys, an indoor bazaar, archway columns and a central 'Alley of Death'/'big banana' lane. Points of interest: faction HQs, Bazaar/Marketplace, Boulevard (western vehicle lane), Plaza and Checkpoint (ruined). Heavy tactical destruction creates new routes and rubble cover. Infantry-only per Fandom infobox; vehicles appear in larger modes.
maps.notes: Official: BF3 Grand Bazaar was 'a very short range close quarter combat map where shotguns tend to be favored'; EA preserves 'classic tight, corridor-driven gameplay'. Reportedly plays 'similar to Hagental Base or Saints Quarter'. Blvd and north-south Bazaar lanes give long sightlines and L115/RPK-74M headshot lanes ('deepest cross-map sightlines'), hence non-trivial LONG. EA says LMs and Rifles can pick players off in the corridor.

maps.name: Contaminated
maps.layout: Mountainside German airbase (Hagental) in the Bavarian Alps; rocky cliffs, tall trees, bunkers. Six Conquest flags: Hagental Village, Zone C Bunker, Hagental Tunnel, Siegfried Line, Pohl Control Center, Maintenance Hangar. Sector flow (EA Operation Augur): Hamlet house+trenches; Siegfried Line bunkers + breachable Hagental Tunnel; Maintenance Hangar trench->hangar; open Ramp/Apron valley staging lane; multi-level climbable bunkers at Hagental Base entrance. VL-7 psychoactive smoke is a mode gimmick.
maps.notes: EA explicitly: 'Contaminated's hillsides and Hagental Base's tunnels demand different loadouts for success.' Ramp/Apron = 'serious long-range duels for valley control' over an otherwise open staging lane; hamlet/tunnel/bunkers = close-quarters breach-and-clear. Size: 'between Eastwood and Mirak Valley', comparable to St. Quentin Scar / Arras (EA). Vehicles: land + helicopters (Fandom also lists jets - flagged inconsistent). inferred: genuinely tri-modal; near-equal split.

maps.name: Eastwood
maps.layout: Southern California golf-resort suburb (Battle of Hunter's Ridge). Five Conquest flags: Suburbs, Neighbourhood, Country Club, Gazebos, Villa. Dense suburban streets (A/B), a central lodge/clubhouse with tiled roofs (Assault Ladder) and destructible walls, an open golf course green at C, a covered car park, hills up to D/E, and swimming pools. Roughly 10 drivable Turfpro PTV golf carts. Vehicles: light/heavy armor + helicopters (no jets).
maps.notes: Documented: 'tight suburban streets around A and especially B', 'open golf course at the back of C', 'a good balance of long streets and open zones where vehicles shine'; TheGamer says it 'leans into a focus on infantry' with cluttered suburban-home capture points. Windows Central calls it the largest game map aside from Operation Firestorm. Supports all combat sizes (EA). inferred: CQB+MID dominant, LONG on the golf course/wide roads.

maps.name: Empire State
maps.layout: Infantry-only Brooklyn, NYC urban map of tight city blocks, L-shaped alleys, side streets, rooftops and tall multi-story buildings with many entry points and windows; destructible interiors/breechable walls. Five Conquest flags: Basketball Court, Construction Zone, Skybridge, Summit Center, Furman Courtyard. Verticality is strong (roofs, skybridge; enemies firing up/down). Winter 'Ice Lock' visual variant. No vehicles.
maps.notes: Documented: 'close, crowded infantry-only... SMGs and shotguns are king'; 'highly vertical urban combat... narrow spaces'; but dblTap notes 'long open stretches for snipers outdoors' while interiors favor shotguns/SMGs. GameWatcher: 'rather open streets around the buildings at the center'. inferred: CQB-dominant with meaningful MID and some LONG on open streets. No vehicle play.

maps.name: Fort Lyndon
maps.size: XL (Battle Royale map; largest Battlefield battleground to date)
maps.layout: Battlefield REDSEC battle-royale map; Southern California/Los Angeles coastal region ('redacted military facility hidden between beaches and a residential community'). 21 named POIs across cities, military bases, industrial landscapes, open wilderness, a golf course, marina/beachfront, hilltops and mountains. Includes full vehicular support (tanks, helicopters, boats/RHIB) and a shrinking wall-of-fire hazard; 100 players. Season 2 added Defense Testing Complex 3 (underground tunnel network).
maps.notes: Worlds: Downtown/Boutique District = dense room-to-room CQB; Chemical Storage/Ground Zero = vertical CQB; Radar Site/mountains/golf fairways/beaches/Marina = long-range; military/industrial compounds = MID. Fandom: largest map since Firestorm's Halvøy; not the same map as Eastwood (EA). inferred: genuinely mixed tri-modal BR sandbox; weights reflect broad spread.

maps.name: Hagental Base
maps.layout: Infantry-only underground base beneath the Bavarian Alps (Hagental Airbase). All action funnels into the wide Central Tunnel (loading area with a huge impact crater and wreckage), plus narrow/deep East and West Tunnels and an intricate tunnel network; areas include Generator, Maintenance, Depot and Server. Unstable ceilings/walls are destructible, collapsing on enemies or opening flank routes. No vehicles.
maps.notes: EA: 'gripping underground close-quarters combat'; CQB users fit Generator/Maintenance/Depot/Server and small rooms/pillars; conversely 'long-range weapon users, such as sniper rifles or LMGs, will find this tunnel - as well as the narrow and deep East/West Tunnels - incredible for their effective range'. Inspiration: Metro, Locker, BF3 Close Quarters. EA calls it 'supporting infantry-only modes'. inferred: most engagements CQB/MID with strong long-lane exceptions.

maps.name: Iberian Offensive
maps.layout: Upper Town, Gibraltar; urban map of winding streets, alleyways, plazas and partly-destructible multi-story buildings with elevation. Five Conquest flags; B Townhouses and C Apartment are the town core, A/D/E are outer vehicle flags. C Apartment has floor-by-floor destruction opening sightlines; D Supply Depot has a flank route and a 'crater of death'. Vehicles: light transports + 1 IFV per side in Conquest (EA blurb and some guides also mention tanks).
maps.notes: Strongest documented dual-range statement: 'emphasizes Close Quarters infantry combat at the capture points within the town (Being B and C), and long-ranged, light vehicle combat at the outer flags (A, D, and E)'. dblTap: 'more open stretches to the sides that allow for sniper gameplay'. PCGamesN: 'winding streets create chokepoints'. inferred: CQB core with real LONG edges and MID plazas.

maps.name: Liberation Peak
maps.layout: Pamir Mountains / Murghob District, Tajikistan; vast rocky mountainside with ridges, valleys, military installations and settlements. Six Conquest flags: Ambush Site, Checkpoint, Ravine Outpost, Village, Vehicle Depot, Command Post. Strong verticality and high-ground advantage; some community sources note caves/tunnels (uncorroborated). Vehicles: light/heavy armor, helicopters, jets.
maps.notes: Documented: 'wide sightlines, steep ridges, and limited cover - making it a haven for long-range players'; 'Long sight lines are also a dream for skilled marksmen'; 'the most open of the beta maps'; 'a favorite for eager snipers'. Infantry can sneak between settlements/buildings, so CQB pockets exist in the central village compound. inferred: LONG-dominant with MID ridge fights and limited CQB.

maps.name: Manhattan Bridge
maps.layout: DUMBO neighbourhood, Brooklyn, NYC; streets beneath and around the Manhattan Bridge, brownstone blocks, bridge underpasses and sides. Destructible structures create new angles; upper deck vs lower underpass lanes; roof access mostly by helicopter. Play space is larger than Empire State. Vehicles: light transports, IFVs, tanks, transport and attack helicopters.
maps.notes: Documented: 'close-quarters map set in the streets below the Manhattan Bridge... weave between cars and buildings with an SMG'; EA: 'close-quarters gunplay on the streets'. PCGamesN: 'the play space is much larger, giving license for vehicles to roam the streets'. BoostRoom: 'vehicles and infantry can both be effective if they respect the narrow lanes'. inferred: CQB-dominant, MID along vehicle streets, LONG only from aircraft.

maps.name: Mirak Valley
maps.layout: Tajikistan valley between two mountain ranges: ruined/destroyed villages, farmlands, a trench system, two construction sites and a central river. Five Conquest flags: Destroyed Village, Construction Site Building (large), Farmland, Construction Site Building (small), Intact Village. Rooftops on the construction buildings are used for sniping/anti-armor; a large crane can be dropped to restrict vehicle movement. Every vehicle type incl. tanks, helicopters and jets.
maps.notes: Documented: 'a wide sandbox, and its central area is open for combat for your vehicles as well as for your planes'; trenches let infantry move 'in relative safety'; construction sites give 'intense CQC' but also long-ranged duels between the two buildings; hilltops watch key bridges. Scale baseline: later Railway to Golmud is ~4x Mirak Valley (TechRadar). inferred: LONG-dominant with CQB islands at construction sites/villages.

maps.name: New Sobek City
maps.layout: Construction yard on the outskirts of Cairo's suburbs; sandwiched between construction sites and massive sand dunes. Five Conquest flags incl. Abandoned Foundations, Housing District, Logistics Outpost (A-C named). Semi-urban construction interiors with cover, stairwells/rooftops for verticality, plus open desert. Vehicles: light/heavy armor, attack helicopters and AA (one of few launch maps with attack helis).
maps.notes: Documented as a genuine split: 'construction yard creates semi-urban fighting while the desert areas let vehicles really stretch their legs'; 'close-quarters construction combat and open-field vehicle warfare'; Radio Times cites 'sniper spots, helicopters, tanks'. GameWatcher calls it the big 'peak Battlefield' experience vs Siege of Cairo's street fights. EA-confirmed rework planned Season 5. inferred: CQB/MID construction + LONG dunes.

maps.name: Operation Firestorm
maps.layout: Balkanabat, Turkmenistan oil refinery (BF3 remake); a huge combined-arms field of wide-open outdoor areas and industrial interior spaces. Five Conquest flags: Logistics Hub, Warehouses, Filling Station, Construction Site, Army Outpost. High smokestacks/distilling tower act as sniper nests with map-wide views; warehouses are tight indoor fight spaces. Vehicles: light/heavy armor, AA, helicopters and jets.
maps.notes: PS.Blog: 'a mix of wide-open outdoor areas, high smokestacks that are great sniper nests, and lots of interior spaces'; 'very long sightlines... and snipers were a major force... that said, both maps have a wide variety of terrain and structures that provide a lot of cover'. Legacy (layout carried to BF6): tight warehouse CQB for shotguns/PDWs, medium between-flag vehicle fights, extremely long sightlines for sniping. inferred: MID+LONG dominant with CQB pockets.

maps.name: Railway to Golmud
maps.size: XL (biggest official BF6 MP map; playable area larger than Mirak Valley)
maps.layout: Reimagined Golmud Railway (BF4) moved to Tajikistan: several square kilometres of ruined village, rolling hills/valleys, an industrial site and a moving train (double engines, cover cars, parkour). Seven Conquest POIs: Construction Site & Village, VIP Compound, Train, Bridge Construction, Warehouse (two multi-story warehouses + elevated walkways), Farm. Expanded airspace/largest jet space to date; added flank routes and cover between objectives.
maps.notes: EA: added 'verticality and flanking opportunities for better engagements at all distances'; train cars invite CQB (SMG/Carbine/Shotgun); Warehouse = 'cat-and-mouse' infantry play; open landscape 'ablaze with tank shootouts'; construction/village rubble gives infantry cover. Dominated by combined-arms vehicles and long-range tank/jet play, with genuine CQB objectives. inferred: broad MID/LONG leaning, meaningful CQB on train/warehouses/village.

maps.name: Saints Quarter
maps.size: Small ('smallest BF6 map by a mile')
maps.layout: Old Town, Gibraltar; close-quarters map built around a central fountain courtyard flanked by destructible houses. Exclusive to CQB modes (no Conquest/Rush/Breakthrough/Escalation); Domination has three flags. Documented focal points: central courtyard, a long side street, and a corner stairwell over a storm drain; second floors and destructible floorboards; the whole area is on a slope.
maps.notes: Documented: 'sightlines are tight, and there's no empty space where vehicles would usually be'; 'combat distances heavily favor close-range weapons. Master your SMG and shotgun skills'; 'layout is fixed to maximise the close combat fights'. Infantry-only. inferred: almost pure CQB with only short MID; zero long-range. (Radio Times' 'full of sniper spots' contradicts primary CQB evidence - flagged outlier.)

maps.name: Siege of Cairo
maps.size: Medium (smaller of the two Egypt maps)
maps.layout: Central Cairo; urban map of tight alleyways and small buildings mixed with large open streets and courtyards, split by a main road running through the middle. Five Conquest flags: Plaza, Palace (interior chambers), Crossing (centre/main road with a crater and bus cover), Souk (courtyard market), Supply Point. Two-storey buildings overlook objectives; destructible walls expose firing angles. Infantry + light/heavy armor (cat-and-mouse with tanks).
maps.notes: Documented: 'cramped alleyways and frenetic indoor skirmishes'; 'you are going to get a lot of close-range fights as well as a lot of indoor fights. The map is filled with choke points'; PC Gamer: 'spaces between objectives are small, sightlines are wide open' (note: wide sightlines are at street scale, hence MID). No documented long-range/sniper reputation; classified relatively small. inferred: CQB-heavy with substantial MID, minimal LONG.

maps.name: Tsuru Reef
maps.size: XL (largest BF6 map at Season 4 launch; archipelago)
maps.layout: Pacific island chain (six main islands) bridging a luxury resort, abandoned harbourside neighbourhood and military base via open ocean and inland waterways. POIs: Majestic Ikoi Resort (hotel/villas + pools), Mifune Landing & Tsuru Gate (central land-bridge island), Tsuru Air Base & Port, Crag Arch, Sunrise Harbor & Moon Shore (U-shaped harbour), Hitode Lagoon, plus NATO/Pax HQs; Mt. Hoshizora is an exposed high vantage. Supports all modes and Naval Warfare (boats, carrier).
maps.notes: EA: resort offers 'a mix of close-quarters and open combat areas, such as outdoor swimming pools and hotel rooms'; Sunrise Harbor 'welcomes close-quarters combat'; Harborside has 'clear sightlines across the island and into open waters'; Hitode Lagoon cliff is 'a great vantage point for long-range firefights'. Extensive open water/air traversal. inferred: balanced tri-modal with strong water/air LONG and CQB at resort/harbour compounds.

maps.name: Wake Island
maps.layout: Horseshoe-shaped Pacific atoll (Wake Atoll), rebuilt for BF6 with Naval Warfare. POIs: Taussig Radar Station, Heel Point Barracks, Hangar One/airstrip, Ammunition & Ordnance Depot, True Energy Hydrocarbons Fuel Storage, Toyoshima Docks, and the new central Shipwreck of the MV Cetus (ziplines). An underground tunnel network links most POIs (Barracks-Hangar, Ammo Depot-Hangar, Ammo Depot-Fuel Storage, Fuel Storage-Docks). Bridges between objectives; capture areas extend into water.
maps.notes: EA: at Taussig Radar Station 'close-quarters weapons thrive within the underground section, while the outdoor areas will be defined by vehicular combat and mid-to-long range infantry gunfights'; Hangar One is 'a large interior space' for CQB or mid-to-long sightlines; Shipwreck/tunnels/buildings = CQB; open water/beaches/bridges = LONG. EA: 'CQB has a home... stick to the underground tunnel network and in between buildings to limit exposure to long-range weapons'. inferred: balanced tri-modal atoll.
